title: fix: explain contested-path holds in commit reports
description: Producer split for task-c2a900aa5107479aa4c630f1b3837ed0. Recorded option B: preserve existing contested-path safety/attribution predicate, add working remediation to reporting/docs. Original parent owns twin launcher held banners, twin postflight regressions, scripts/CLAUDE.md and final integration/hardening. In recordCommit.ts recognize validated skipped entries with exact MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED or MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(<peer>) code shape; append bounded held-path/remedy line to task-channel report and trigger existing rate-limited governors alert even for committed/nothing with zero unattributed paths. Use skipped, not contested trailers: a contested path may have landed via TOOL, and must not be falsely reported held. Preserve ledger/path unions/duplicate semantics; chat errors remain best-effort. Remedy: declare_files does not override contest; after verifying bytes are this task's and coordinating any live peer, an owning assignee's landing session must produce a wrapper-observed successful editing-tool witness (currently Claude stream-collected Edit/Write, not shell writes), or legitimately complete/archive the stale peer before retry. Never claim declaration, plain unblocking, or arbitrary shell touch alone solves it. Update declareFiles.ts tool description/new-path message with contest caveat, docs/MCP_SERVER.md corresponding contract passages, and docs/roles/governor.md cheat sheet without loosening safety. Tests in recordCommit.test.ts cover alert/code classification/truncation/repeat window/chat failure and declare_files output caveat. Own exactly those five files. No new wire field/schema or wrapper edits. Dependencies serialize shared MCP docs only. Root verification: (cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test) && npm run lint.
definitionOfDone: A held contested skipped entry produces bounded actionable task-channel and rate-limited governors messages for committed and nothing outcomes without requiring unattributedPaths; regression tests assert both.
Contested-but-landed trailer entries, unrelated/near-match skip codes, and malformed skipped entries do not produce false held alerts; repeat-window and chat-error behavior remain compatible.
declare_files still unions paths exactly as before, but description/success prose and docs/MCP_SERVER.md accurately state declaration does not bypass contested holds.
docs/roles/governor.md states the verified-assignee-session TOOL or legitimate terminal-peer remedy, not declaration/plain unblocking/shell touch as a guaranteed bypass.
Fresh (cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test) && npm run lint exits 0; attribution decision and state-file/tool input contracts are unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
Held contested paths in record_commit (recordCommit.ts), test-first. Load test-driven-development: write the step-1 tests in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/recordCommit.test.ts, watch them fail, then implement. The decision is option B, from Serena decision-declare-files-contested-hold: report and explain the hold. The attribution predicate does not change and nothing bypasses the hold.

1. Classify a skipped entry as HELD only from its code. It is never inferred from `contested`: a contested path that a witness or `contested: commit` landed also appears there, with a Moe-Contested trailer. Work on the readRecordList output, which has non-blank trimmed strings capped at 255 chars and at most 100 entries. Add a pure helper, `heldContestedPaths(skipped, contested)`, that never throws:
   - code exactly 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED' (strict attribution.contested=skip): peer = the taskId of the `contested` entry whose path normalizes to the same path, else null;
   - code exactly matching /^MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED\((task-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\)$/ (skip-untouched): peer = the captured id;
   - every other code is ignored: other MOE_ATTR_* codes, lowercase, a missing or empty peer, a peer without the task- prefix, trailing characters after ')', nested parens, a space inside;
   - normalize the path with the existing PathSet / tolerantNormalizePath from util/attributionTiers. A path they drop (absolute, traversal, non-string) is malformed and ignored;
   - dedupe by normalized path, first entry wins, keeping its peer and kind.
2. When at least one path is held, append ONE line to `lines`, for every outcome (a NO_OWNED_PATHS refusal is often exactly this case):
   `MOE_CONTESTED_HELD task=<id>: <path>(<peer or ?>), … (+N more) — <remedy>`
   - Show at most HELD_PATHS_SHOWN = 5 entries, the same bound as the wrapper's held= suffix; N counts the remaining distinct paths.
   - The remedy is constant text, so the line stays bounded.
   - If any entry is skip-untouched, the remedy says: verify these bytes are this task's and coordinate any live peer; then either this task's own assignee session edits the path with a wrapper-observed successful editing tool (Claude Edit/Write family or a supported Serena editor, not a shell write), or the stale peer task is legitimately completed or archived, before the next landing. declare_files, unblocking or a shell touch alone does not release it.
   - If any entry is strict, the remedy adds: attribution.contested=skip holds the path whatever the session's tools did; only resolving or legitimately finishing the peer task releases it. Never change the policy as the fix.
3. alertGovernors also becomes true when the held list is non-empty, so committed and nothing outcomes alert with zero unattributedPaths. The alert goes through the existing 24h per-task window, which every alert reason shares. Do not change the ledger, the path unions, duplicate detection, lastCommitOutcome, warnings or the response shape: no new wire or response field and no schema change. Chat stays best-effort, so error handling is unchanged: both posts keep their try/catch, and a failed post never changes the stored outcome.

Tests (new describe block in recordCommit.test.ts, reusing seed/record and the postSystemMessage/postToRoleChannel spies):
1. committed + skipped [{ path: 'src/held.ts', code: 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-peer)' }], no unattributedPaths: the task line contains 'MOE_CONTESTED_HELD task=task-1: src/held.ts(task-peer)' and the editing-tool remedy text. #governors gets that line once.
2. outcome nothing + a strict 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED' entry whose path appears in contested with taskId 'task-peer2': shows 'src/strict.ts(task-peer2)' and the strict remedy; governors are alerted. A strict entry with no matching contested entry shows '(?)'.
3. Contested but landed: contested [{ path: 'src/b.ts', taskId: 'task-peer' }] with paths ['src/b.ts'] and no contested skip code gives no held line and no governors call.
4. it.each near-match and unrelated codes give no held line and no alert on a clean committed record: 'MOE_ATTR_PEER_DECLARED', 'MOE_ATTR_PREEXISTING', 'moe_attr_contested', 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTEDX', 'XMOE_ATTR_CONTESTED', 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED', 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED()', 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(peer)', 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-a)x', 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-a)(task-b)', 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-a b)'.
5. Malformed entries alongside a valid code give no held line, and success is still true: a string, null, an array, a missing path, a blank code, a numeric path, an absolute path '/etc/x', and a traversal '../x'.
6. Truncation: 7 distinct held paths plus one duplicate show exactly 5 '(task-peer)' items, then '(+2 more)'.
7. Repeat window: a second held record for task-1 inside the window posts the task line again but makes no second governors call. task-2 alerts on its own. After resetRecordCommitGovernorRateLimit, task-1 alerts again. A held alert and an unattributed alert for the same task share one window.
8. Chat failure: both spies reject, the record still resolves success true, and commits and lastCommitOutcome are stored.
9. Ledger unchanged: the same committed record with and without held skipped entries stores equal commits[0] (ignoring recordedAt), filesModified, inferredPaths and unattributedPaths.

declare_files caveat (declareFiles.ts), prose only, test-first.

1. The tool description currently says the wrapper commits declared paths 'regardless of the pre-task baseline'. Keep that, and add the caveat: declaring does not override a contested hold. A declared path that another nonterminal task also declares is still held at landing (MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(<peer>) / MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED), and record_commit's MOE_CONTESTED_HELD line names the remedy.
2. The success message for new paths ('Declared N new path(s) on <task>; the wrapper commits them under the task on its next exit.') must gain the same short caveat: '…unless another open task also declares one (a contested hold; declaring does not release it).' Keep the 'already declared' message as it is, because declareFiles.test.ts asserts it.
3. Do NOT change path validation, normalization, the union, alreadyDeclared, the activity event, the chat post, the response keys, or any error handling path.

Tests (in recordCommit.test.ts, because the task owns exactly that test file; declareFiles.test.ts must pass unchanged):
- the declareFilesTool description mentions the contested hold and that declaring does not release it (assert distinctive substrings);
- declaring ['src/a.ts'], then ['src/a.ts', 'src/b.ts'], gives declaredFiles ['src/a.ts', 'src/b.ts'], addedPaths ['src/b.ts'] and alreadyDeclared ['src/a.ts'] exactly as before, and the second message contains the caveat;
- a fully repeated declaration still says 'already declared'.

Contract docs (docs/MCP_SERVER.md, record_commit and declare_files sections only).

First run git diff -- docs/MCP_SERVER.md. Hunks you did not write belong to other tasks: as of 2026-10-27, task-cd2e4477's unlanded finalTaskId text, plus whatever the prerequisites task-0b40957c and task-9a9b46d8 add. Never revert, reformat or stage them, and name them in your step note. Edit with the built-in Edit tool, which is the TOOL witness for this contested path.

1. record_commit, Notes 'Chat:' bullet:
- #governors is now also alerted when a skipped entry is a held contested path, through the same once-per-task-per-24h window.
- Classification comes from skipped codes only: exactly MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED, or MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-<peer>). `contested` alone is never taken as a hold, because a witnessed or `contested: commit` path lands with a Moe-Contested trailer.
- The line format is MOE_CONTESTED_HELD task=<id>: <path>(<peer>) …, with at most 5 paths, then +N more, then the remedy.
- Strict-skip remedy: a peer resolution only, no TOOL bypass.
- Skip-untouched remedy: verify ownership, coordinate the peer, then either a wrapper-observed successful editing-tool write in the owning assignee's session (see docs/CONFIGURATION.md attribution.contested for the supported tools), or a legitimately finished peer, before retrying.
- Declaration, plain unblocking and a shell touch are not fixes, and neither is changing the policy.
- The response, the stored records and the inputs are unchanged.
2. declare_files:
- In the first paragraph, 'commits them regardless of the baseline' gains 'unless another nonterminal task also declares the path'.
- Add a Notes bullet: declaring never overrides attribution.contested. A path that another open task declares is still held (the codes above), and record_commit's MOE_CONTESTED_HELD line names the remedy.

Governor cheat sheet (docs/roles/governor.md), then regenerate its vendored copy.

1. Add a signal-table row after MOE_ATTRIBUTION_UNRESOLVED:
- Signal: `MOE_CONTESTED_HELD`.
- Source: `record_commit` (task channel; #governors once per task per 24h).
- Meaning: the landing held a path this task owns because another nonterminal task also declares it.
- Action: verify the bytes are this task's and coordinate the live peer. Then either the owning assignee's own Claude session edits the path with a wrapper-observed editing tool before its next exit (a shell write leaves no witness), or the stale peer task is legitimately completed or archived and the landing retried. Under `MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED` (attribution.contested=skip) only the peer route works. Declaring, plain unblocking or touching the file from a shell does not release it, and never change the policy as the fix.
2. Amend the three existing declare_files mentions so none promises a landing for a contested path: the MOE_ATTRIBUTION_UNRESOLVED row, workflow step 3's declare_files entry, and escalation step 4. Add a short clause pointing at the MOE_CONTESTED_HELD row. Keep everything else, including the reference doc, untouched.
3. Regenerate packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts with `npm run generate-init-files` in packages/moe-daemon. HEAD keeps every role doc's marker sha in that file equal to docs/roles (verified 2026-10-27 for all 8 docs), and the JetBrains plugin stamps the same sha at runtime: a stale entry makes the plugin and the daemon overwrite each other's copy of the doc.
- Run the generator where git history and a working tsx both exist: Windows Git Bash in the real checkout (its node_modules are Windows-native). Never run it from a git-archive snapshot: the shipped-body sha list reads `git log`, and without it the list shrinks.
- Error handling: if the generator fails, or the diff touches anything other than the governor.md entry (its body, its marker sha, and one new shipped-body sha), stop and report it rather than hand-editing the generated file.
- Then run npm run lint from the repo root (the role-doc cap; governor.md is exempt but the test still runs).

Verification gate, run once. From the repository root, run exactly: (cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test) && npm run lint. It must exit 0. Submit the command, exitCode and outputTail (the vitest totals plus the lint OK lines) to moe.complete_task.

Environment:
- Under WSL the shared checkout's node_modules are Windows-native, and vitest dies with 'Cannot find native binding'. Run the whole command from Windows Git Bash at the repo root, which also gives npm run lint its bash.
- Or run the daemon half in a Linux snapshot per Serena gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate: git archive HEAD of the whole repo, overlay ONLY this task's six paths, symlink a native node_modules, MOE_* unset, and cmp the six files before citing the run.
- Never npm install in the shared checkout.
- tsconfig excludes *.test.ts, so tsc does not type-check the test file; vitest runs it.

This task changes no schema, migration, wire field or tool input, so the daemon suite plus the lint is its full regression.

Adversarial self-review, run once. Load adversarial-self-review and read the diff of your six paths as an attacker:
- False holds: can a contested-but-landed path, a near-match code, a lowercase code, a missing peer, an absolute or traversal path, or a non-object entry produce MOE_CONTESTED_HELD?
- Missed holds: does a held path on committed, nothing, refused and failed outcomes, with zero unattributedPaths, always produce the line, and on committed/nothing the alert?
- Boundedness: are there at most 5 paths, constant remedy text, capped fields, and no unbounded join?
- Rate limit: is it one governors alert per task per window, whatever the reason? Does a clean committed record still alert nobody?
- Error handling: rejected chat posts never fail the call or change the ledger, and the helper cannot throw on any input.
- Contract: no response field, stored field or input changed; the declareFiles union is byte-identical; and declareFiles.test.ts and the existing recordCommit tests pass unchanged.
- Wording: nothing in the code, docs or governor row says that declaration, unblocking, a shell touch or a policy change releases a hold. The strict code never suggests a TOOL bypass. The remedy names the owning assignee's own session.
- Generated file: initFiles.ts differs from HEAD only in the governor.md entry.

Mutation probe, on a scratch copy or reverted at once: drop the held clause from alertGovernors, then accept the bare 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED'. Confirm a test fails for each. If the review changes bytes, rerun the step-5 command and submit only fresh exit-0 evidence.

comments.author: architect-1520cc31
comments.content: Important policy nuance for reporting tests: MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED means strict attribution.contested=skip; a TOOL witness does NOT bypass it. Only MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(peer) under skip-untouched can suggest the verified successful editing-tool witness. For strict skip say resolve/legitimately finish the peer before retry. Never imply a shell touch or mere unblocking works, and never change the policy as remediation.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Choices made, with the rejected alternatives:
1. Option B is kept, per Serena decision-declare-files-contested-hold: report and explain the hold, with no DECLARED bypass and no predicate change.
2. Holds come from skipped codes, not the contested list. The contested list also names paths that landed through a TOOL witness or contested=commit, so using it would raise false held alerts.
3. No response or ledger field, because the task says no new wire field or schema. The wrapper discards record_commit's response anyway.
4. The line goes on every outcome. It matters most on a MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_NO_OWNED_PATHS refusal whose only owned path was held, where it explains the refusal.
5. One shared 24h window for every alert reason. Adding a second window would double-page governors.
6. The bound is 5 shown paths, matching the wrapper's held= suffix, instead of UNRESOLVED_PATHS_SHOWN (20).
7. initFiles.ts is regenerated even though the description lists five files. HEAD keeps all 8 role-doc marker shas in sync with docs/roles (checked), and a stale entry makes the plugin and the daemon overwrite each other's copy. The sixth file floors the plan to the heavy tier, so the plan runs on Opus at the xhigh floor. Leaving the vendored copy stale was rejected.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
What the code does today:
- Wrapper sh python (moe-agent.sh about lines 3660-3676, ps1 twin about lines 3581-3599) emits skipped codes 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED' (policy skip) and 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(<peer taskId>)' (skip-untouched, no TOOL witness, not idle-clean). `contested` gets (peer, path) for EVERY contested path, landed or held. The record_commit payload sends skipped as {path, code} (MOE_ATTR_EXCLUDED filtered out, at most 100) and contested as {path, taskId}.
- attr_held_list (sh) and Get-MoeHeldList (ps1) already format <path>(<peer>), at most 5 then +N more, for the session-ended held= suffix. The strict code's peer is looked up in contested by path.
- The TOOL witness is Claude stream-collected only: Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit plus Serena editors (replace_content, replace_symbol_body, insert_*, create_text_file, line editors, replace_regex; safe_delete_symbol only on OK; rename_symbol only for its declaring file; replace_in_files only for the files it lists). Codex/gemini/grok have no TOOL set.
- recordCommit.ts: readRecordList trims and caps; skipped is only counted in the line, never stored. alertGovernors is unattributed || rescueLanded || refused/failed, with governorAlertAt as the per-task 24h Map plus a reset seam.
- declareFiles.test.ts asserts only 'already declared' in the message.
- lint-role-docs.sh caps only architect/worker/qa at 40 lines.
- generate-init-files reads docs/roles + docs/agents and runs git log for the shipped-body shas; docs/roles, docs/agents and generated/ are clean now.
planningNotes.risks:
Risks for the worker to watch:
- dependsOn task-0b40957c and task-9a9b46d8 serialize docs/MCP_SERVER.md: expect their hunks there.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md also carries task-cd2e4477's unlanded hunks and is contested (task-72184c65). Use the Edit tool. A codex/gemini/grok seat's edit to it is held. Name foreign hunks for attribution and never stage or revert them.
- Regenerate initFiles.ts only where git history and a Windows tsx work. A WSL run of tsx fails (Windows build), and a snapshot lacks .git.
- The remedy wording is the DoD. Per the architect-1520cc31 comment, MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED must never suggest a TOOL witness.
- readRecordList trims codes, so a whitespace-padded exact code counts. That is acceptable, because padding is not a near-match after the reader's normalization.
- governorAlertAt is module-global: every test resets it in beforeEach, as the file already does.
